content: Method comparison and recommender-pick presentation follows a consistent pattern across ML leaderboards and model selection tools: (1) run all candidates on same data and record per-metric scores; (2) rank candidates per metric; (3) pick a winner using either single-metric ordering or weighted aggregation; (4) justify by citing the winning metric value and the margin over the runner-up. Key design decisions for grounded comparative advisors: (a) winner selection must be based on fdars-computed scalars, not LLM judgment; (b) the LLM role is to narrate WHY the winner is better, citing numeric margins; (c) present a per-metric rank table alongside narrative; (d) flag ties and near-ties explicitly (margin < threshold); (e) note when no single method dominates across all metrics. The champion/candidate pattern from production ML: always compare new candidate against current best, only promote if better by threshold on primary metric. For FDA method selection (e.g. FPC-LM vs PLS vs kernel), the comparison surface needs: method name, primary diagnostic value per method (e.g. cv_error_rate), rank, margin to next-best.
